borrower.label: Borrower
borrower.description: Seeks the financing and describes the project: completes the project's steps.

funder.label: Funder
funder.description: Considers financing the project: reviews what the borrower has entered.

intermediary.label: Intermediary
intermediary.description: Supports the borrower, e.g. designing the transaction: can complete the financial and project steps with them.

landowner.label: Landowner / Habitat Bank
landowner.description: Owns the site and runs the habitat bank: registers it, plans its management and decides on unit reservation requests.

investor.label: Investor
investor.description: Invests in the habitat bank and shares its revenue: agrees unit pricing and decides on reservation requests with the landowner.

developer.label: Developer
developer.description: Builds the development and buys the units it needs: completes the development's steps and reserves off-site units.

ecologist.label: Ecologist
ecologist.description: Surveys habitats, runs the biodiversity metric and verifies monitoring reports.

lpa.label: Local Planning Authority
lpa.description: Approves legal security, planning permission and the biodiversity gain plan; verifies monitoring reports.

fields.name: disclaimer_text
fields.content:
The information provided through this platform may be used to support biodiversity assessments, nature-based solution development, financing activities, stakeholder engagement, research, reporting, and other objectives related to BioFin-EU.

Project information may be shared with authorised stakeholders, funding organisations, project partners, and other participants within the BioFin ecosystem where necessary to support project evaluation, collaboration, financing, monitoring, and reporting activities. Users may opt out of certain data-sharing activities by adjusting the settings below, although some information required for the operation, administration, security, and legal compliance of the platform may continue to be processed and retained.

While reasonable efforts are made to ensure the accuracy and integrity of information contained within the platform, users remain responsible for verifying the completeness and correctness of any data they provide or rely upon. Information, methodologies, indicators, and platform functionality may be updated, revised, or enhanced over time.

By proceeding, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this notice and consent to the collection, processing, storage, and use of your information in accordance with the BIOFIN platform's operational requirements and applicable data protection regulations.

fields.name: allow_data_sharing

fields.help_text: Lets BioFin share this project's information with relevant stakeholders, project partners and potential funding organisations, as described in the disclaimer.

fields.name: name
fields.help_text: A short name that identifies this project across the platform, for example in the project list.

fields.name: high_level_description
fields.help_text: A brief summary of the project: what it involves, where it takes place and what it aims to achieve for nature.

fields.name: locations
fields.help_text: The site(s) the project covers. Draw each site as a polygon on the map, or enter a point. The country is detected automatically, and each polygon is used to assess its biodiversity risk in the Vulnerability Index.

entry_help_text.friendly_name: A friendly name you choose for this location, such as “North field” or “Riverside plot”, so you can tell your sites apart when a project has several. It’s used to label the location on the project dashboard and in the Vulnerability Index.

fields.name: loan_amount
fields.help_text: The total loan amount requested, in the currency selected below.

fields.name: currency
fields.help_text: The currency used for the amounts in this step.

fields.name: use_of_proceeds_id
fields.help_text: What the money will mainly be spent on, for example farm machinery, working capital or land purchase.

fields.name: nature_positive_percentage
fields.help_text: The share of the loan, from 0 to 100%, that goes to activities with a positive impact on nature, such as habitat restoration or more sustainable land management.

fields.name: notes
fields.help_text: Anything else about the financing that reviewers should know.

fields.name: organic_farmer_number
fields.help_text: The farm's organic certification or registration number, if it is certified organic.

fields.name: environment_scheme_number
fields.help_text: Your agreement or reference number in an agri-environment or nature scheme, if you take part in one.

fields.name: subsidy_reference
fields.help_text: The reference of any public subsidy or grant linked to this land or project.

fields.name: registry_notes
fields.help_text: Extra context about the identifiers above, for example which registry or scheme each one belongs to.

fields.name: assignments
fields.help_text: The organisations supporting this project and the role each one plays. Add one row per intermediary and function; an intermediary can hold more than one function.

row_fields.name: intermediary_id
row_fields.help_text: An organisation registered on the platform that supports the project, for example by designing the transaction, recruiting investors or coordinating restoration work.

row_fields.name: intermediary_function_id
row_fields.help_text: The role this intermediary plays in the project. Only the functions registered for the chosen intermediary are listed.

fields.name: name
fields.help_text: A short name that identifies this project across the platform, for example in the project list.

fields.name: high_level_description
fields.help_text: A brief summary of the project: what it involves, where it takes place and what it aims to achieve for nature.

fields.name: financing_type_id
fields.help_text: How the project will be financed: private, public, hybrid or blended finance, or philanthropic funding.

fields.name: locations
fields.help_text: The site(s) the project covers. Draw each site as a polygon on the map, or enter a point. The country is detected automatically, and each polygon is used to assess its biodiversity risk in the Vulnerability Index.

entry_help_text.friendly_name: A friendly name you choose for this location, such as “North field” or “Riverside plot”, so you can tell your sites apart when a project has several. It’s used to label the location on the project dashboard and in the Vulnerability Index.

fields.name: nbs_environment_type_id
fields.help_text: The type of ecosystem the solution is in, for example cropland, forest, grassland, wetland, rivers and lakes, coastal or urban. Choose Multiple when it spans several.

fields.name: nbs_intervention_type_id
fields.help_text: The specific kind of intervention, for example protecting and conserving ecosystems, managing agricultural landscapes or restoring degraded ecosystems. Only interventions that fit the environment are offered, grouped by type: 1, better use of existing natural ecosystems; 2, managed or restored ecosystems; 3, new ecosystems.

fields.name: nbs_approach_type_id
fields.help_text: The overall approach the solution takes, for example ecological restoration, green infrastructure or ecosystem-based adaptation. Only approaches that fit the intervention are offered.

fields.name: nbs_societal_challenge_type_id
fields.help_text: The main societal challenge the solution helps address, for example climate resilience, water management, food security or human health. Only challenges the intervention addresses are offered.

fields.name: implementation_stage_id
fields.help_text: How far along the project is, from concept and feasibility through pilot and scaling to operational and maintenance.

fields.name: nbs_description
fields.help_text: Describe the solution in your own words: what will be done on the ground and how it benefits nature and people.

fields.name: funding_amount
fields.help_text: The total funding the project needs. It must equal direct funding plus indirect funding.

fields.name: currency
fields.help_text: The currency used for the amounts in this step.

fields.name: upfront_costs
fields.help_text: One-off costs to set the project up, such as land preparation, planting or construction.

fields.name: maintenance_costs
fields.help_text: Ongoing costs to keep the solution working over time, such as monitoring, upkeep and management.

fields.name: direct_funding_amount
fields.help_text: Funding that goes directly to the project. Direct plus indirect funding must add up to the funding amount.

fields.name: indirect_funding_amount
fields.help_text: Funding that supports the project indirectly, for example through partners or linked programmes. Direct plus indirect funding must add up to the funding amount.

fields.name: funding_notes
fields.help_text: Anything else about the funding needs, such as timing, phasing or conditions.

fields.name: nature_positive_benefits
fields.help_text: The benefits for nature the project is expected to deliver, for example more habitat, species or ecosystem services. Be as specific and measurable as you can.

fields.name: legislation_compliance
fields.help_text: How the project meets or goes beyond relevant laws and standards, such as environmental or land-use regulations.

fields.name: additional_rationale
fields.help_text: Any other reasons an investor should support this project, such as social benefits, co-funding or track record.

fields.name: supporting_document
fields.display_name: Supporting documents, proof of meeting standards
fields.help_text: Upload evidence that supports the application, such as certificates, surveys, plans or proof of meeting relevant standards.

fields.name: document_notes
fields.help_text: Explain what the uploaded document is and what it shows.

fields.name: name
fields.help_text: A short name that identifies this habitat bank across the platform, for example in the project list.

fields.name: high_level_description
fields.help_text: A brief summary of the habitat bank: what it involves, where it is and what it aims to achieve.

fields.name: landowner_name
fields.help_text: The person or organisation that owns the land.

fields.name: ownership_type
fields.help_text: How the landowner holds the land.

fields.name: land_registry_title
fields.help_text: The HM Land Registry title number(s) for the site, if registered.

fields.name: supply_role
fields.help_text: How this site will supply biodiversity units.

options.value: Habitat bank selling units to developments
options.label: Habitat bank selling units to developments

options.value: Landowner supplying units for a specific development
options.label: Landowner supplying units for a specific development

fields.name: contact_email
fields.help_text: Who to contact about this habitat bank.

fields.name: locations
fields.help_text: The boundary of the land being registered as a habitat bank. Draw it as one or more polygons on the map.

entry_help_text.friendly_name: A friendly name you choose for this area, such as “North field”, so you can tell several areas apart.

fields.name: ecological_feasibility
fields.help_text: Whether the planned habitats can realistically be created or improved here, given soils, hydrology and surroundings.

fields.name: additionality
fields.help_text: Why the gains are additional: they must go beyond what the land is already required to deliver (for example by other schemes or legal obligations).

fields.name: constraints
fields.help_text: Anything that limits what can be done, such as designations, access, rights of way or contamination.

fields.name: commercial_viability
fields.help_text: Whether selling units is likely to cover the costs of creating and managing the habitats for 30 years.

fields.name: bng_eligible
fields.help_text: Your conclusion on whether the site is suitable to supply BNG units.

fields.name: parcels
fields.help_text: The habitats on the site today, from an ecological survey. Record each parcel of area habitat (hectares), hedgerow (km) and watercourse (km) with its condition. (Simplified prototype metric, not the Statutory Biodiversity Metric.)

fields.name: metric_notes
fields.help_text: Anything to note about the baseline, such as survey dates or assumptions.

fields.name: parcels
fields.help_text: The habitats the site will have once creation and enhancement works are complete. The uplift over the baseline is what the habitat bank can sell as units. (Simplified prototype metric, not the Statutory Biodiversity Metric.)

fields.name: management_period_years
fields.help_text: How long the habitats will be managed and monitored. BNG requires at least 30 years.

fields.name: management_summary
fields.help_text: How the habitats will be created and then maintained, for example grazing, cutting or planting regimes.

fields.name: monitoring_frequency
fields.help_text: How often progress will be monitored and reported.

fields.name: reporting_obligations
fields.help_text: What will be reported, to whom and when.

fields.name: price_per_habitat_unit
fields.help_text: What a development pays for one area habitat unit from this habitat bank.

fields.name: price_per_hedgerow_unit
fields.help_text: What a development pays for one hedgerow unit. Leave empty if the bank has no hedgerow uplift.

fields.name: price_per_watercourse_unit
fields.help_text: What a development pays for one watercourse unit. Leave empty if the bank has no watercourse uplift.

fields.name: delivery_cost
fields.help_text: The expected total cost of creating the habitats and managing and monitoring them for 30 years. Used to compare against the revenue from selling units.

fields.name: landowner_share_percent
fields.help_text: The landowner's percentage of every sale of units. The three shares must add up to 100%.

fields.name: investor_share_percent
fields.help_text: The investor's percentage of every sale, for example to repay the cost of creating the habitats. Enter 0 if there is no investor.

fields.name: manager_share_percent
fields.help_text: The percentage for whoever manages and monitors the habitats for 30 years. Enter 0 if the landowner does this.

fields.name: pricing_notes
fields.help_text: Anything else about pricing, such as discounts or indexation.

fields.name: agreement_type
fields.help_text: The legal agreement that secures the habitats for at least 30 years.

fields.name: agreement_reference
fields.help_text: The reference of the signed agreement.

fields.name: agreement_date
fields.help_text: When the agreement was signed.

fields.name: responsible_body
fields.help_text: The local planning authority or responsible body that holds the agreement.

fields.name: register_reference
fields.help_text: The site's reference on Natural England's biodiversity gain sites register.

fields.name: registration_date
fields.help_text: When the site was added to the register.

fields.name: register_notes
fields.help_text: Anything else about the registration.

fields.name: name
fields.help_text: A short name that identifies this development across the platform, for example in the project list.

fields.name: high_level_description
fields.help_text: A brief summary of the development: what it involves, where it is and what it aims to achieve.

fields.name: planning_authority
fields.help_text: The council that will decide the planning application.

fields.name: development_type
fields.help_text: The main kind of development.

fields.name: planning_reference
fields.help_text: The planning application reference, if one exists yet.

fields.name: locations
fields.help_text: The boundary of the development site. Draw it as one or more polygons on the map.

entry_help_text.friendly_name: A friendly name you choose for this area, such as “North field”, so you can tell several areas apart.

fields.name: parcels
fields.help_text: The habitats on the development site before any works, from an ecological survey. (Simplified prototype metric, not the Statutory Biodiversity Metric.)

fields.name: parcels
fields.help_text: The habitats that will be on the site after development, including any created or enhanced on-site. Compared with the baseline, this shows the losses and the gain still needed. (Simplified prototype metric, not the Statutory Biodiversity Metric.)

fields.name: avoid
fields.help_text: How the design avoids harm to habitats, for example by keeping valuable areas out of the development.

fields.name: minimise
fields.help_text: How unavoidable harm is reduced.

fields.name: restore
fields.help_text: How damaged habitats will be restored on-site.

fields.name: residual_impacts
fields.help_text: Harm that remains after avoiding, minimising and restoring, which must be compensated.

fields.name: onsite_decision
fields.help_text: Whether the 10% net gain can be met on-site, or off-site units are needed for the shortfall shown above.

fields.name: decision_notes
fields.help_text: The reasons for the decision.

fields.name: allocations
fields.help_text: Request units from registered habitat banks to cover the shortfall. The habitat bank accepts or declines each request; accepted units are reserved for this development, become allocated when planning permission is granted, and are retired when the gain plan is approved.

fields.name: application_reference
fields.help_text: The planning application reference.

fields.name: submission_date
fields.help_text: When the application was submitted.

fields.name: bng_documents
fields.help_text: The ecological reports, metric and BNG proposals submitted with the application.

fields.name: decision
fields.help_text: The planning authority's decision. When permission is granted, the development's reserved off-site units become allocated. To refuse the application, use Reject: it goes back to the developer.

fields.name: decision_date
fields.help_text: When the decision was issued.

fields.name: conditions_summary
fields.help_text: A summary of any conditions attached to the permission.

fields.name: condition_reference
fields.help_text: The reference of the statutory pre-commencement biodiversity gain condition.

fields.name: condition_notes
fields.help_text: Anything else about the condition.

fields.name: gain_plan_reference
fields.help_text: The reference of the approved biodiversity gain plan. Approving it retires the allocated off-site units (they can never be used again) and creates a transaction record for each.

fields.name: approval_date
fields.help_text: When the gain plan was approved.

fields.name: approval_notes
fields.help_text: Anything else about the approval.

fields.name: commencement_date
fields.help_text: When development started on site.

fields.name: commencement_notes
fields.help_text: Anything else about the start of works.
